info.title: blindfold API
info.description:
An API for playing and watching turn-based games without a screen. All game logic runs on the server. Client developer guide: `/guide.md`.

`turn` is the number of actions applied so far. Send the current `turn` with each action; otherwise it is rejected with `STALE_TURN`.
A room goes `waiting` -> `playing` -> `finished`.

bearerAuth.description: The player `token` from `POST /rooms/{id}/join` or `POST /quickmatch` (`hostToken` for `start`). `?token=` in the URL is rejected.

rulesVersion.description: Version of the game's rules (an integer, bumped whenever a change could make an old log replay differently). Rooms created with an older version (waiting, in progress or finished) fail with GAME_REMOVED

viewVersion.description: Version of the shape of view (an integer, bumped when a view field is removed, renamed, changes type or meaning, or gets a new value in a fixed set; not when a field is added)

hasOptions.description: True if the game takes gameOptions (see optionsSchema in its rules)

viewSchema.description: JSON Schema of view (fields that only some viewers receive are optional). Does not forbid extra fields: new ones may be added

optionsSchema.description: JSON Schema of gameOptions (POST /rooms), or null if the game has no options. Unknown keys are rejected

defaultGameOptions.description: gameOptions used when none are given (null if the game has no options)

options.description: Markdown: meaning of each game option. null if the game has no options

stateExamples.description: Example state messages generated from the engine: start, after one action (each viewer), finished

endExample.description: The end message that follows the finished example

common.description: Markdown: how to play, common to all games (turn, legal, errors)

gameOptions.description: Game-specific options of the room (defaults filled in). null for games without options

status.description: Same as status in the room state. Currently one of `waiting`, `playing`; more values may be added.

players.description: Number of players who have joined

maxPlayers.description: Number of seats in this room (its `seats` option, default the game's maxPlayers)

autoStart.description: If true, the game starts by itself once the room is full

rulesVersion.description: Rules version of this room, recorded when the room was created. If the game's rulesVersion goes up, the room fails with GAME_REMOVED

gameOptions.description: Game-specific options of this room (defaults filled in; see optionsSchema in /games/{id}/rules). null for games without options

status.description: Room lifecycle. Treat an unknown value as neither waiting nor finished: keep listening for the next state. Currently one of `waiting`, `playing`, `finished`; more values may be added.

turn.description: Number of actions applied so far. Send this value with your action

view.description: Game-specific board as seen by the caller (hidden information removed). Its JSON Schema is viewSchema in /games/{id}/rules. null while waiting

legal.description: Present only if the caller may act now and the game lists legal moves (listsLegalActions in /games). Whether you may act is decided by currentPlayers, not by legal

deadline.description: Deadline of the current turn (epoch ms, server clock). null unless playing

phaseTurn.description: The turn at which the current turn began. On a simultaneous turn, turn goes up each time someone acts but phaseTurn stays the same; otherwise it equals turn. If you sent an action with a turn >= phaseTurn and you are still in currentPlayers, this state was built before your action was processed: wait for the next state instead of acting again. null unless playing

now.description: Server clock (epoch ms) when this response was built. Time left = deadline - now (do not use the client's clock)

roomId.description: The new room. Call POST /rooms/{id}/rematch on this (finished) room to take your seat there

requestedBy.description: Players of this room who have asked for the rematch

rematch.description: Present only after the game has finished and someone asked for a rematch

rulesVersion.description: Rules version the game was played with. If it differs from rulesVersion in /games/{id}/rules, the rules changed later and /replay is no longer available for this game

gameOptions.description: Game-specific options the game was played with (defaults filled in). null for games without options

actions.description: Every entry in turn order; actions[i].turn === i

turn.description: The turn this entry was applied at (0, 1, 2, ...). Applying it produced turn + 1

player.description: Who acted. null for a timeout or resignation entry (written by the server)

action.description: The action as sent (an element of legal). null for a timeout or resignation entry

at.description: When it was applied (epoch ms, server clock)

timeout.description: Present only on a timeout entry: the players who ran out of time

resign.description: Present only on a resignation entry: the player who resigned

rulesVersion.description: Rules version the game was played with (always the current one; older games fail with GAME_REMOVED)

allOf.description: The log entry that produced this frame (= actions[turn - 1] of /log). null for the first frame (turn 0)

frames.description: frames[i].turn === i. The first frame is the initial position, the last one the final position

stats.description: Counts over recorded (non-practice) games joined with this user's X-Api-Key

id.description: Same as the roomId of the game (so /rooms/{id}/log and /replay work with it until the finished room is deleted, 7 days after the end)

rulesVersion.description: Rules version the game was played with

gameOptions.description: Game-specific options the game was played with (defaults filled in). null for games without options

reason.description: Why the game ended. normal = decided by the game's rules. Treat an unknown value like normal. Currently one of `normal`, `timeout`, `resign`; more values may be added.

userId.description: The user who joined with X-Api-Key, or null

outcome.description: draw only for a game decided as a draw by its rules. If everyone timed out, everyone gets loss. Treat an unknown value as neither a win nor a loss. Currently one of `win`, `loss`, `draw`; more values may be added.

score.description: scores[playerId] of the result, or null if the game has no scores

get.description: Rules, how to read `view`, the JSON Schemas of `view` and `action`, example states, and how to play (common to all games). The same content as one Markdown page: `/games/{id}/rules.md`.

post.description: `options.turnTimeMs` (1000-86400000) sets the time limit per turn; the default is 5 minutes. By default a player who times out loses. `options.seats` (between the game's minPlayers and maxPlayers; default maxPlayers) is the number of seats: the room is full at that many players. With `options.practice: true`, server-side practice bots fill the empty seats (up to `seats`, or minPlayers if `seats` is omitted) when the game starts (how they play depends on the game; practice games are not recorded). With `options.autoStart: true`, the game starts as soon as the room is full (cannot be combined with practice). Rooms are listed in `GET /rooms` by default; pass `options.unlisted: true` to hide a room (practice rooms are never listed). Unknown options are rejected with 400. `gameOptions` are options specific to the game (see `optionsSchema` in `/games/{id}/rules`; games without options reject them with 400). Defaults are filled in and recorded with the room, its log and its match. The returned `hostToken` is needed to start the game (`/rooms/{id}/start`); only the creator has it.

turnTimeMs.description: Time limit per turn in ms (default 300000 = 5 minutes)

seats.description: Number of seats, between the game's minPlayers and maxPlayers (default maxPlayers). The room is full, and autoStart starts it, at this many players; practice fills the empty seats up to it

practice.description: Fill empty seats (up to seats, or minPlayers if seats is omitted) with server-side practice bots at start. Not recorded in results

autoStart.description: Start automatically once the room is full (seats, default maxPlayers). Cannot be combined with practice

unlisted.description: Hide from GET /rooms and quick match; only people who know roomId can join

gameOptions.description: Options specific to the game, matching optionsSchema in /games/{id}/rules. Omit for the defaults. Games without options reject any value

hostToken.description: The creator's token for starting the game. Not a player token

get.description: `status=waiting` (default): waiting rooms with a free seat, updated within the last 30 minutes. `status=playing`: games in progress (for spectating), as long as the room has shown activity within its time per turn plus 2 hours. Finished games are in `/matches`. Unlisted and practice rooms are never listed. The list is an index and may lag: if a join fails with `ROOM_FULL` or similar, try the next room.

post.description: Joins the oldest public auto-start room of the same game, game options, turn time and number of seats that has a free seat, or creates such a room (`autoStart: true`) and joins it. The game starts by itself once the room is full, so connect the WebSocket with the returned `token` right away and wait (you receive `status: "waiting"` states, then `playing`). `created` tells whether a new room was created. No `hostToken` is returned (nobody can start early). Send `X-Api-Key` to record the result on your user.

gameOptions.description: Options specific to the game, matching optionsSchema in /games/{id}/rules. Omit for the defaults. Games without options reject any value

post.description: Player IDs are assigned in join order: p1, p2, ... (numbers of seats that were left are not reused). Seat order (= `players`) is the turn order. Rematch rooms cannot be joined here (`ROOM_RESERVED` 403; use `POST /rooms/{id}/rematch` on the finished room). Send `X-Api-Key` to record the result on that user; a user can take only one seat per room (`ALREADY_JOINED` 409). A waiting room is deleted 24 hours after its last join or leave.

post.description: A secondary option. REST has no way to wait for the other players, so use the WebSocket (`/rooms/{id}/ws`) to play a full game. Do not poll `/state` (it uses up the free-tier request budget). If `turn` is not the current turn, the action is rejected with `STALE_TURN` (409), except that on a simultaneous turn an older `turn` of the same simultaneous turn is accepted while the player may still act. An action that arrives after the deadline also gets `STALE_TURN`, after the timeout is resolved on the spot.

post.description: Allowed at any time while the game is playing, even when it is not your turn. By default the resigning player loses, all other players win, and the game ends immediately (some games define their own handling). Over the WebSocket, send `{"type":"resign"}`. Before the start or after the end: `NOT_PLAYING` (409). It cannot be undone.

post.description: Call it on the finished room with your player token. The first call creates a new room with the same game and options; every call seats the caller there and returns the new `roomId`, `playerId` and `token`. Seats are rotated by one (in a two-player game, first and second player swap). Only the players of this room can take those seats (others get `ROOM_RESERVED` 403). The new game starts by itself once every player has called rematch (practice bots are added again at start). Calling again (also after leaving the new room) returns the same seat and token. The finished room's `state` gets `rematch: { roomId, requestedBy }`, pushed over the WebSocket, so the other players can see the offer (`requestedBy` lists everyone who has asked at least once). The others may never answer: if the new room does not start within a time you choose, leave it. To decline after accepting, leave the new room (`POST /rooms/{newId}/leave`). Before the end: `NOT_FINISHED` 403.

get.description:
To connect as a player, pass the subprotocols `["blindfold.v1", "blindfold.token.<token>"]` (e.g. `new WebSocket(url, ["blindfold.v1", "blindfold.token." + token])`). The server answers with the `blindfold.v1` subprotocol. Clients that can set headers may send `Authorization: Bearer` instead of the token subprotocol. The `blindfold.v1` subprotocol (the version of the WebSocket messages) is required, also for spectators and with Bearer. Without a token you are a spectator. `?token=` is rejected with 400.

Connections are limited: up to 4 per token (one more closes the oldest with close code 4004) and 50 spectators per room (503 `TOO_MANY_CONNECTIONS`). A socket that receives more than 20 errors in a burst (one is forgiven every 10 s) is closed with close code 4003.

Server -> client: `state` / `error` / `end` / `pong`. Client -> server: `{"type":"action","turn":N,"action":{...}}`, `{"type":"resign"}` and `{"type":"ping"}`.

post.description: Send the current key as `X-Api-Key`. The response has a new `apiKey` (returned only once) and the old key is rejected from then on. Use it when a key may have leaked; to revoke a key, rotate it and keep the new one secret. Seats already taken with the old key keep recording their results. If the key is lost, the user cannot be recovered: register a new one.
